Safety · Rain · 13:30 JST

“Extratropical” is not an all-clear.

A tropical cyclone changes category when its structure changes. Moisture can still feed a front, rivers can rise after local rain eases, and landslide risk can persist in saturated slopes.

Japanese word of the day警戒 · けいかい · keikai

Vigilance; caution; being on alert. 警 means “warning,” while 戒 means “to guard against.” It appears in weather, wildlife and public-safety reporting, and asks for prepared attention rather than panic.

Example: 土砂災害に警戒してください—“Please remain alert for landslides.” Today, the word matters even after Typhoon 30 lost its typhoon classification. Practice Japanese free in the Japanese Training Lab, then learn while playing with DraMap for iOS.
